findings.title: Findings converge on the framework instance-name mapping
findings.why_it_matters: Two representations of framework across four tables, with the rule owned in two places.
findings.choice_reason: Asked first why framework rows exist when no peer was said to have them; adopted one write-side owner, and framework keys skip the name filter.

findings.title: The index-to-name lookup returns __hassette__ for framework keys, but log and blocking rows store NULL
findings.why_it_matters: A per-instance log or blocking query for a framework key returns empty with no error.
findings.recommended: A: No name filter for framework keys on log and blocking queries

findings.title: Nothing says where a framework owner's None becomes __hassette__
findings.why_it_matters: An obvious conversion would file an app-tier None under the framework name and merge sibling rows.
findings.recommended: A: Telemetry-name property on Resource, overridden by App

findings.title: D1's live set doesn't say where names come from, and the sweep's surroundings still assume bare app keys
findings.why_it_matters: A name missing from the live set retires a running instance's rows, and the retirement log line becomes false for a rename.
findings.recommended: A: Specify the source, keep keys for the prune, log pairs
findings.chosen: A: Specify the source, keep keys for the prune, log pairs

findings.title: Migration 018's default value and UPDATE predicates are unstated
findings.why_it_matters: Rows both UPDATEs miss keep the default, and a collision makes the unique index fail on every boot.
findings.chosen: State DEFAULT '__unset__' and split the UPDATEs on source_tier

findings.title: Seed generators and test doubles are missing from the change list
findings.why_it_matters: The client_compat claim depends on doubles the ledger doesn't list, whose responses could go empty.
findings.chosen: Add a Summary bullet naming fixtures and doubles

findings.title: Renaming back restores history is unqualified
findings.why_it_matters: Retention can delete the old row, so a returning name starts fresh after a retention-length delay.
findings.chosen: Qualify the docs bullet with retention

findings.title: An index held from before a reorder resolves to a different instance until #3100
findings.why_it_matters: Index-addressed views stay positional until #3100, showing another instance with no signal.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation

findings.title: D1 sweep granularity versus one-hour stale rows
GET /logs/recent?instance_index=N without app_key now answers 422, and the ledger misdescribes what it replaced
findings.why_it_matters: A request that returned every app's logs at that index now gets validation_failed, while the ledger says no API change and that the route ignored the index.
findings.recommended: A: Keep the 422 and correct the record
findings.chosen: A: Keep the 422 and correct the record
findings.choice_reason: Applied without the responses= declaration the option named: validation_failed is a global code and problem_responses rejects declaring it, so the fix corrects the ledger only.

findings.title: The test meant to pin migration 018's framework non-collision cannot fail on the real risk
findings.why_it_matters: The test only inserts index-0 framework rows, so it passes whatever the real invariant is, while its docstring claims to pin it.
findings.recommended: A: Keep 018; make the test prove the failure mode
findings.chosen: A: Keep 018; make the test prove the failure mode

findings.title: Per-instance log and blocking filters lose rows recorded before names were required, which the ledger doesn't state
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: users with long retention histories. Rows from before #3095 hold derived names, so they drop out of per-instance results until retention removes them.
findings.recommended: C: Accept as a known limitation
findings.chosen: C: Accept as a known limitation

findings.title: A directly constructed App stores instance_name = "", which stored_instance_name doesn't refuse
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: any user who builds an App outside config loading. Two such apps under one app_key silently overwrite each other's telemetry rows.
findings.recommended: C: Accept as a known limitation
findings.chosen: A: Treat falsy names as missing
findings.choice_reason: Sounds like the one line check fix is worth it? Or is there a downside I'm not seeing

findings.title: The retention sweep decides from a live-set snapshot taken before its transaction starts
findings.why_it_matters: The sweep and registration writes run on one sequential worker, so no upsert can land between the snapshot and the UPDATE.

findings.title: Blocking-finding instance refs merge by name but report whichever index was seen first
findings.why_it_matters: The query orders newest first, so setdefault already keeps the newest index.

findings.title: Silent-empty on a stale index is inferred from live registry state at request time
findings.why_it_matters: The keep-the-index decision's ratified sentence accepts this behavior until #3100.

findings.title: Retention sweep could retire everything from a momentarily empty or partial manifest set
findings.why_it_matters: reload() validates first and swaps config synchronously, so the sweep can't see a half-swapped config.
